question:
What will be the direction of the force based on the direction of current and magnetic field as shown in the figure?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09930db2796331c9efa47bccd2efc48dc94603581721de00321b61903716a8e9.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __Out of the page__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Given: an electron moves to the right (this is the direction of velocity) and the magnetic field is directed downward.
 
• Magnetic force law: the magnetic part of the Lorentz force is F = q (v × B). This means the force direction is determined by the vector cross product of velocity (v) and magnetic field (B), then multiplied by the charge (q).
 
• Compute v × B: direction of v is to the right, direction of B is down. Using the right-hand rule for the cross product (thumb = v, fingers = B), v × B points into the page.
 
• Effect of negative charge: an electron has q , so the force is opposite to the direction of v × B. Since v × B is into the page, the magnetic force on the electron is out of the page.
 
• Conclusion: combining the cross product result with the negative sign of the electron yields the net force out of the page. This is why the correct answer is Out of the page.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor:**

 
 
• The magnetic force (also called Lorentz force) is experienced by a conductor carrying electric current when placed in a magnetic field.
 
• The magnitude of the force is given by the formula: **F = BIL sin θ**, where:
 
 
• **B**: Magnetic field strength (in Tesla).
 
• **I**: Current in the conductor (in Amperes).
 
• **L**: Length of the conductor (in meters).
 
• **θ**: Angle between the magnetic field and the current direction.
 
 
 
• The direction of the force is determined using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Magnetic Force:**
 
 
• The concept is used in **electric motors** to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy.
 
• It is also applied in **generators, loudspeakers, and electromagnetic devices.**
 
• The principle is crucial in designing devices that rely on the motion of conductors in magnetic fields.
 
 
 
• **Real-life Examples:**
 
 
• **Electric motors:** The rotating armature in motors uses the magnetic force to generate torque.
 
• **Maglev trains:** Magnetic levitation relies on electromagnetic forces to reduce friction and allow high-speed travel.
 
• **Particle accelerators:** Charged particles are directed using magnetic fields in research applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnetic Field:**

 
 
• A magnetic field is the region around a magnet or current-carrying conductor where magnetic forces can be experienced.
 
• The magnetic field lines are visualized as moving from the **north pole to the south pole** outside the magnet.
 
 
 
• **Electric Current:**
 
 
• It is the flow of electric charge (usually electrons) in a conductor.
 
• Current direction is conventionally taken as the direction of positive charge flow.
 
 
 
• **Interaction of Magnetic Field and Current:**
 
 
• The force arises due to the interaction of the magnetic field with the moving charges in the conductor.
 
• This interaction is a fundamental principle in electromagnetism, explaining how electric and magnetic phenomena are interrelated.
